Getting started

Open the space

Click the Tandem icon in the activity bar (left edge) to browse your repositories and their thinking spaces, then run Tandem: Open the Space (or click a space in the tree) to open it. Each thinking space opens in its own editor tab, titled with that space’s name — opening one leaves every other space’s tab open, so several can be open side by side.

If your workspace has more than one folder, Tandem asks which repository you are working on — it never guesses. The choice shows in the status bar ("Tandem: <repo>") and can be changed any time from there, from the <repo> ▾ button in the map, or with Tandem: Switch Project / Repository. Each repository gets its own space.

Say what you want

Type into the capture box, in your own words, as many lines as you need (Enter sends; Shift+Enter breaks a line). What you type is classified:

  • an ask ("add a clear button to the toolbar") is grounded — the machine reads the repository and comes back with changes: sentences, the files they land in, and acceptance criteria;

  • a question ("where does the toolbar render?") gets an answer and is recorded nowhere;

  • a statement ("we always deploy through the platform CI") becomes a decision in force that every later derivation builds under.

Decide what the code cannot

If the repository supports more than one reading of your ask, a question appears with a recommended answer. Press Accept to take the recommendation, or edit it first — your wording wins. The decision re-grounds the ask immediately and rides every later worker brief. Questions never block silently, and the sign gate refuses a cut whose asks still have open questions.

Cut and sign

Add units to the cut. If the grouping is wrong, pin: Merge into one slice or Split out. The cut screen shows what ships, what it needs first, and refuses to sign anything unprovable or ungrounded. Sign mints your TEP with a content-bound approval token — edit anything under the signature and the token stops matching until you sign again.

Watch it build, then accept

The run starts on its own; see The run and the orchestration graph. When the delivery arrives, its page lists every proof (green or red, with evidence) and every UNDELIVERED item. Accept merges it on your forge; a delivery with a red proof, or with an unmet documentation obligation, refuses to be accepted.
